page: Amazon Web Services x8i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs based on 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The processor is an Intel Xeon 6975P-C running at 3.9 GHz, equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled, and the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows strong performance in memory and computational tasks. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2173.0 and a multi-core score of 19574.0, with top-tier performance in image processing and text processing. Memory bandwidth tests recorded a strong 3831.46 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, though large-block uncached reads and writes fell into the average range at 172.41 GB/sec and 73.25 GB/sec, respectively. In database operations, the server demonstrated strong capabilities with a PassMark database score of 22611.51 and 90.13 million operations per second in Redis SET tests.

The Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions for integer and tile operations. These hardware features translate to strong LLM inference speeds, processing 3735.82 tokens per second for small models and 29.97 tokens per second for large models during prompt processing. However, text generation speeds for larger models are more moderate, averaging 2.9 tokens per second for a 70B model. Given the high DDR5 memory density and strong database and decompression benchmarks, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
